title: 測量学Ⅱ
subtitle: Surveying II
keywords: Registered surveyors 2.GNSS, GIS, RS 3.Mapping, geography 4.Flip teaching 5.3D surveying simulation
educationalGoal: In Surveying II, students learn about spatial information technologies such as GIS, GNSS, and RS, which are new surveying fields. Specifically, the course covers traverse surveying, GNSS surveying, and geographic information systems. Some subjects will be instructed using flipped teaching.
advice: (1) Students will learn traverse surveying; calculation of azimuths, bearings, latitudes and departures, adjustments to latitudes and departures, total latitude and total departure, and area. These are taught using flipped teaching (active learning) e-learning. (2) Students will do traverse survey exercises using a 3D simulator (active learning) (3) Students will do GIS (geographic information system) exercises using QGIS (active learning) (4) Students will become acquainted with other spatial information technologies (GNSS (GPS), laser surveying, etc.) (5) Students will do national examination exercises on topics 1 to 4 listed above (related to national qualifications) (6) Students will create exam question candidates in cooperation with senior SA (active learning).
requiredKnowledge: This subject is indispensable preparation for Surveying Practicum/Exercise I and II and Spatial Information Technology. Students can acquire practical skills by taking Surveying Practicum/Exercise I and II. Students can create Excel calculation sheets that they can apply it to many survey calculations. The Power Point slides used in the lecture will be posted on the e-syllabus. This course is closely related to the Registered Surveyor examination.

activityGoals.body: Students can explain the principles of, equipment used, and characteristics of various surveying methods (0.1L)
Students can select survey methods correctly depending on the terrain and purpose of the survey. (0.1L)
Students can deepen their knowledge of spatial information technology and design/planning. (0.1M, 0.1H)
Students can solve basic and applied problems that appear on national exams for registered surveyors (0.1L, 0.1)
Students can explain the importance of surveying and spatial information engineering(0.1L, 0.1M)
Students can actively involved in flipped learning, including questions in collaboration with SA. (0.1L, 0.1M)

achievementLevels.ideal: In traverse surveying, students understand azimuth, bearing, latitude and distance, and accurately calculate error and area. They can create a data calculation sheet with Excel. They can explain raster data and vector data in GIS and positioning methods in GNSS in detail. Students understand the details of the coordinate reference system, spatial data collection and measurement methods, and can explaine mesh code of map management. They can solve advanced application problems from registered and assistant surveyors’ national tests. They can also create exam and practice question candidates in cooperation with senior SA.
achievementLevels.standard: In traverse surveying, students understand azimuth, bearing, latitude and distance. They understand the concepts of spatial information technology and understand the three fields (GIS, GNSS, remote sensing) that make up spatial information engineering. They understand the Japanese coordinate reference system, spatial data collection and measurement methods and mesh coding. They can solve basic problems from registered and assistant surveyors’ national tests. Students can do temporary tutoring.
